data.name: Mujtahid
data.gender_notes: Mujtahid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is qualified to issue legal rulings and interpret Islamic law. The name Mujtahid carries the meaning “Jurist, Scholar” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mujtahid usually hope their child will grow to embody jurist, scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of wisdom and knowledge, a seeker of truth and justice.
data.etymology: Mujtahid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jurist, Scholar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mujtahid total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The title of Mujtahid holds great significance in Islamic culture as it is a title of respect and admiration for those who have attained a high level of expertise in Islamic law and jurisprudence. These individuals are religious scholars who have dedicated their lives to studying and interpreting Islamic law, and their rulings and fatwas (legal opinions) are often followed by millions of Muslims around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the title of Mujtahid represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom in the service of God. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking truth and understanding the divine law, and the responsibility to apply that law in a just and compassionate manner. For a Mujtahid, the quest for knowledge is not just a personal endeavor, but a sacred duty to serve the greater good of the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Jurist, Scholar" symbolizes One who is qualified to issue legal rulings and interpret Islamic law.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mujtahid serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of jurist, scholar.
